html:
SMTO-HTTP-0030 — SMTO couldn't find the web address it tried to reach

GUID: 3201ddba-edde-44f2-93e0-2aa53f928eed
Slug: http-dns-failed
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • The Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses to run work on a computer) couldn't look up the name of the website or service, so the request never reached it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store, select the HTTP connection the task uses, and check Base URL for typos, such as a missing letter or .com instead of .net. One wrong character turns the address into a name that doesn't exist anywhere.
  2. If the connection uses a proxy, open Advanced connection settings and check HTTP proxy URL and HTTPS proxy URL the same way. SMTO has to look up the proxy's name too, and a mistyped proxy name fails the same way.
  3. Make sure the computer running the Gateway is connected to the network and can open the same address in a web browser. The name is looked up on the Gateway's computer, so its network connection decides whether it can be found.
  4. Select Test connection on the HTTP connection. When it shows Reachable, run the task again. The test confirms the address can be found before the task tries again.

What success looks like

  • Test connection shows Reachable, and the task's web request gets an answer.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the address you expected SMTO to reach, to the person who manages your network or SMTO. Don't swap in a different, unchecked address just to make the error go away.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway's HTTP client failed name resolution (socket.gaierror) for the destination or proxy hostname, so no connection was established.

What this means

  • The transport exception chain contains socket.gaierror, indicating a name-resolution failure on the actual Gateway route. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The transport exception chain contains socket.gaierror, indicating a name-resolution failure on the actual Gateway route.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the destination or configured proxy hostname and the Gateway's resolver route; the label alone does not identify which hostname failed.

How to fix it

  • Verify the hostname in the HTTP connection profile's base_url and in proxy.http/proxy.https, then confirm it resolves on the Gateway host (for example with getent hosts or nslookup) and fix that host's resolver, VPN or split-DNS settings.
  • Correct the failing destination or proxy hostname and restore name resolution on the selected Gateway.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended destination/proxy name resolves on the selected Gateway.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
